definition: An adaptive learning-rate optimization algorithm that combines momentum with per-parameter learning-rate scaling.
details: Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation) is one of the most widely used optimizers for training deep neural networks, including large language models, due to its fast convergence and relatively low tuning burden.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Adam Optimizer.

citation.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
